citations.quote: If literal-1 is specified, compilation-variable-name-1 references literal-1.
If literal-1 is specified, compilation-variable-name-1 references literal-1.

cases.reason: DEFINE format: 2002 operand is arithmetic-expression-1 | literal-1 | PARAMETER [OVERRIDE] | OFF; 2023 adds boolean-expression-1 (widening, not literal-1). Literal categories (numeric fixed-point, alphanumeric incl. hexadecimal, national, boolean) are the same; floating-point barred by 7.2.2 SR10 in both. A DEFINE cannot be on a 2002 debugging line (7.2.2 SR8 d), so no debugging reach; no CD reach.
cases.widening: 2023 adds boolean-expression-1 to the DEFINE format (its own GR7); GR8 itself unchanged

evidence-2002.numeric: covered by probe eval_basic.cob at --std 2002 (DEF-NUM-OK, DEF-FRAC-OK)

flags-answered.behaviour-switch: compile-time-arithmeti: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301), read only by CompileTimeArithmetic.For (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs:44), which picks the mode for operand entry and + - * / inside a compile-time arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1; its 34-digit 2002 mode against §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1's 32 digits is the known PB5575-family defect, reaching only results of arithmetic operations). A single numeric literal operand of DEFINE is a literal, not an arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.9.3 GR5), so literal-1 never enters the arithmetic mode the switch selects. Re-run now at --std 2002: eval_basic.cob prints DEF-NUM-OK, DEF-ALNUM-OK, DEF-BOOL-OK, DEF-NAT-OK and DEF-FRAC-OK (1.5 kept, where an arithmetic expression would be truncated to its integer part by §2002:7.2.5.2 GR2) (E:\COBOL-coord\scratch\op-20261114\read-2002\out-answer\probes-a-03\run-evalbasic-2002.log).

flags-answered.behaviour-switch: compile-time-arithmeti: The switch (DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined, src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs#For) picks only the mode in which a compile-time arithmetic expression is evaluated: Standard at 2002, as §2002:7.2.5.2 GR1 requires ('Standard arithmetic shall be used for all arithmetic operations'). cases.reason: A single numeric literal is never evaluated, so neither the arithmetic-mode difference nor the integer truncation (2002 7.2.5.2 GR2 = 2023 7.3.6.3 GR3) reaches it. The 31-digit numeric literal limit is the same in both editions. Extra probes at both editions: the signed literal -1.5 matches WHEN -1.5 and not WHEN -1; a 31-digit fraction (0.000...001) is kept; a fractional THRU bound (4.5 THRU 5.5) holds. All gave identical output at 2002 and 2023.
